Project Mímir

Free · Open source · Project-based

Learn to build AI agents, from zero to hired

Project Mímir is a free, open-source curriculum for becoming an AI engineer. Written lessons, the best free resources on the internet, and a real project every few lessons that goes straight into your portfolio.

Start with Foundations How it works

8 paths · 167 lessons · 42 portfolio projects

The curriculum

  1. 00

    Foundations

    Set up a real developer environment, learn Python, Git and how the web works, then build your first app on a language model.

    42 lessons · 8 projects
    ~200 hours
  2. 01

    AI Engineering Core

    The everyday skills of an AI engineer: prompting, structured outputs, backends, retrieval, and, most important, evals.

    25 lessons · 6 projects
    ~300 hours
  3. 02

    Agentic Systems

    The heart of the curriculum. Build agents from scratch, learn when not to, connect them to the world with tools and MCP, and make them safe and measurable.

    39 lessons · 10 projects
    ~300 hours
  4. 03

    Production & LLMOps

    Take your work from "runs on my laptop" to "runs for real users": deployed, observable, affordable and secure.

    12 lessons · 4 projects
    ~120 hours
  5. 04

    ML Foundations Elective

    Optional, but recommended. Understand what's under the hood. It makes you better at debugging, at choosing between fine-tuning and prompting, and in interviews.

    13 lessons · 4 projects
    ~150 hours
  6. 05

    Research Track Elective

    Optional, and recommended for anyone heading to a master's or a research role. The theory behind agents: math, reinforcement learning, planning, multi-agent systems, and how to read, run and write research.

    22 lessons · 5 projects
    ~200 hours
  7. 06

    Final Capstone

    Pick a real problem for a real user, then build, evaluate, deploy and write it up. This becomes the centerpiece of your portfolio.

    3 lessons · 1 projects
    ~100 hours
  8. 07

    Getting Hired

    Turn your skills into a job. Learn the roles, build a portfolio that proves you can do them, and prepare for interviews.

    11 lessons · 4 projects
    ~80 hours

Who it's for

  • AI Engineer

    Builds LLM features into products: retrieval, structured extraction, evals and APIs.

  • Agent Engineer

    Designs tools and agent loops that complete multi-step work on their own.

  • AI Solutions Engineer

    Works with customers to turn messy workflows into working AI systems.

  • Master's & research

    The Research Track covers the math, RL, planning and research skills a degree expects.

Frequently asked questions

Is Project Mímir really free?

Yes. Every lesson is free, and every linked resource is free to read or watch. The only cost is a few dollars of AI model usage for some projects, and free local models work for nearly everything.

Do I need coding experience to start?

No. The Foundations path starts from zero: the terminal, Git, Python, how the web works and how language models work. If you already code, skim Foundations and use its projects to test yourself.

How long does it take to finish?

The core paths take about 1,100 hours, roughly 12 to 18 months at 15 to 20 hours a week. Two optional electives, ML Foundations and the Research Track, add about 350 hours.

What jobs does it prepare me for?

Applied AI roles: AI engineer, agent or automation engineer, forward-deployed or AI solutions engineer, and LLMOps engineer. The Research Track adds the theory needed for a master's degree or research work.

How is Project Mímir different from a course or a bootcamp?

It follows the method of The Odin Project: one ordered path, written lessons that link the best free material instead of recording new lectures, and a project you build and publish on GitHub every few lessons.

Project Mímir is free and open source, inspired by The Odin Project (not affiliated). Found a broken link or a better resource? Contribute on GitHub.
